issue.title: test_process_group_kill_reaps_grandchildren_and_resistant_children races a non-atomic pid-file write: exists() is true before the digits land, so int('') raises under the parallel lane
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY closed epic phase sase-p3.12 (epic sase-p3, plugin-extensible task bead types) at 2026-08-18T04:58:57Z: "tests/test_procs_supervisor.py::test_process_group_kill_reaps_grandchildren_and_resistant_children failed once in the escalated suite with ValueError empty int, then passed on rerun — flaky, not caused by this phase." Routed here by sase-p3.15.land while resuming sase-p3's interrupted landing. Every other follow-up that epic left open already had a bead (sase-jb, sase-pr, sase-pg, sase-oz, sase-oh); this node did not, and unlike those it is not carried in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, so nothing absorbs it today.

ROOT CAUSE, read directly out of the test at HEAD 11f78656d — this is a non-atomic-write race in the test itself, not scheduler contention:

```python
deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
while time.monotonic() < deadline and not grandchild_pid.exists():
    time.sleep(0.05)  # sase-test-wait: poll grandchild pid file
gpid = int(grandchild_pid.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))   # tests/test_procs_supervisor.py:138
```

The subprocess writes the grandchild pid with `pathlib.Path(...).write_text(str(child))`, which is `open()` + `write()` + `close()`, not an atomic replace. `Path.exists()` flips to True the instant `open()` creates the inode, which is strictly before the digits are written. If the poll observes the file in that window, `read_text()` returns `""` and `int("")` raises `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''` — exactly the reported signature. Under the full parallel lane the writer is descheduled between create and write far more often, which is why this only ever shows up in the escalated suite.

Two smaller defects in the same block, worth fixing in the same pass:
1. The loop has no post-condition assertion. If the 10s deadline expires with no file at all, the failure surfaces as a bare `FileNotFoundError` from `read_text()` rather than a message naming the timeout, so the two distinct causes are indistinguishable in a CI log.
2. `is_process_running(gpid)` on the next line would be handed a garbage pid if a partial write ever produced a short-but-parseable number. A partial numeric read is possible in principle for a multi-digit pid, and would make the test assert against an unrelated process.

SCOPE: make the handshake atomic and the wait explicit. Preferred fix is to have the subprocess write to a temp path in the same directory and `os.replace()` it onto the final path, so `exists()` implies fully written; alternatively, poll for parseable content instead of mere existence (read, strip, retry while empty) and assert the deadline was met before parsing. Do not simply widen the 10s deadline — the deadline is not what fails here.

This is a test-only defect. src/sase/procs/spawn.py:193 does its own `int(payload["pid"])`, but that reads an already-parsed JSON payload, not a racing file, and is not implicated.

task_type_fields.evidence: Observed once by epic phase sase-p3.12 on 2026-08-18 in the escalated (full-suite parallel) lane of `just check`, failing with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''`; passed on rerun on the same unchanged tree. Fail rate is low — one observation across that phase's runs — and it has not been seen serially: the node passes reliably in isolation, which matches the diagnosed root cause, because the create-then-write window the test races against is only wide enough to lose when the writing subprocess is descheduled under a full-width xdist lane. The diff under test when it failed was the sase-github `github` task type and issue-mirror stamping, which touches no procs, supervisor, or process-group code, so it is not attributable to that change. Not carried in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt at HEAD 11f78656d, so the flake-baseline gate does not absorb it. Root cause is diagnosed from source rather than inferred from timing alone: tests/test_procs_supervisor.py:135-138 polls `Path.exists()` and then `int(read_text())`, while the writer uses non-atomic `write_text`, so an empty read is reachable whenever the poll lands between `open()` and `write()`.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: .venv/bin/python tools/run_pytest default tests/test_procs_supervisor.py (passes serially; only observed in the full parallel lane)

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-or — 'Replace the remaining multiprocessing-fork and os.fork sites in the test suite with in-process seams'. This test is one of the os.fork sites that bead would sweep, but the two defects are different and either can be fixed without the other: sase-or is about forking from the multi-threaded pytest process inheriting only the calling thread, whereas this node's fork happens inside a spawned  subprocess and the actual failure is the non-atomic pid-file handshake back to the parent. If sase-or lands first and replaces this fork with an in-process seam, check whether the pid handshake survives in the rewrite before closing this one.

RELATED: sase-lk — 'Flaky under the full parallel lane: three tests/monitor/test_monitor_supervise.py rows whose pipe does not EOF promptly'. Same subsystem family (supervisor process-group teardown under load) and same lane, but a different mechanism: sase-lk is about a pipe that never EOFs, this one is a file-write race in the test's own setup. Worth reading together by whoever hardens supervisor teardown tests.
